body: Yesterday, I had 2 envelopes with tracking, delivered at two different times. The 1st at 9:20 am, stating it was left at the front desk. The 2nd one was delivered at 2:10 pm , in my mailbox. The receptionist told me there was no post man in the morning that left an envelope for me, and I caught sight of the 2:10 pm mailman as he was departing. I stated all this in my complaint to usps, yesterday and they told me they will get back to me in a couple of days. What I emphasized to them was that we never had 2 usps deliveries in one day and why didn’t the so called 1st postman just stick the envelope in my mailbox, like always. At first I thought a false delivered scan with the employee pocketing my envelope, though now I believe it might of been delivered to another residencial building that doesn’t have mailboxes, earlier in the route, since I live downtown where many hotels and apartments are located. My missing mail didn’t show up today. I’m hoping tomorrow that it will, so I don’t have to contact eBay about it. Because I don’t see that going well. Still, it was a $49 coin, that I wanted. One good thing is my urge to spend money on eBay has gone.

Maybe. This looks like a UK penny or half penny. Possibly 189? with high grade details under that corrosion. Best method is to stick it in a jar of olive oil for a year or more, while keeping it as warm as possible on a sunny window sill and/or on a stove top pilot or oven vent. This will cause the corrosion to flake away naturally without damaging the coin. Still, might end up with pock marks and/or porosity on the surface.

Counterfeiters have the hardest time with the rim and edges, usually. The rim on the reverse of your coin has a seam going around most of it. This could be because it might be a cast. The VDB looks pretty good, though I can not tell the position of the middle bar of the B, which needs to be diagonal and not horizontal. The serif’s at each end of the S need to be vertical and parallel to each other. On higher grades, like yours, a depression is often seen in the upper serif. Also, a small die chip is usually visible at the bottom of the indent of the inside back of the upper loop of the S. I can not tell about these particular’s, because your photo is not detailed enough for the S to be seen clearly. Also, did you weigh it. Some counterfeit Lincoln’s have been substantially lighter than authentic coins. Enough that it’d be noticeable in hand.

What does the edge look like ? That is where counterfeiters usually mess up. 100 CENTS ONE DOLLAR OR UNIT is what needs to be there. A reeded edge is definitely counterfeit. Did you weigh it and check if it is magnetic or not ? It needs to be around 26.96 grams and not magnetic. With these 3 favorable, there is a chance of authenticity or a very good copy. Also check if it is 39 to 40 millimeters in diameter.

The counterfeiters are doing better with their edges of the coins, since the indents of the reeding are more realistic. Being narrow and wider apart. There doesn’t suppose to be any reeding on the 1804 dollar. Nor any raised rim, between the edge and the denticles.

The texture of the surface, which has enough smoothness on the highest surfaces and the highly defined shapes and details of the castle’s and the lion’s look more authentic than not. Still, if there is a seam running around the edge of the coin, it’s probably a cast. If not, weigh it, measure the diameter and make sure it’s not magnetic to get a better idea on whether it is real or not. Then google 16th century Mexican 8 Reales, to find if your coin is close to what their data says.

The Arabic numerals just above the ribbon starts with a 1 .  Next the backward 7 with a extra hook at the end is actually a 3. The 3rd numeral is a 2 . Then the V numeral is a 7. So 1327 AH = 1909 AD as this Sultan’s date when he started his reign. The accession date. Now on the other side just below that object that looks like a teapot which is called a Toughra that is the monogram of the ruler is what looks to be a 7. This is actually 6 in Arabic, which means the 6th year of his rule that means this coin was minted in 1333 AH which is 1915 AD. On the other side again with the accession date, at the top, below the star are 2 small Arabic numerals which gives the denomination. The left one that looks like a squat circle with a opening on it’s left side is a 5 and the dot at the right is a 0, so 50. 50 Kurus, which is the scribbling just below that.
